script.base: Book expects a one-score DAL lead in a moderate 43.5 game, not a shootout or a 38-point clock-kill. DAL's weeks 4-6 identity is pass-first (Lamb 45 targets, Pickens 27, Flournoy 19) and PHI blitzes only 25%, the split where Dak's EPA is 0.17 rather than 0.02. PHI's QB is 0.00 EPA unblitzed and -0.26 vs blitz, and the run game is a Pierce/Bigsby/Shipley split at 2.13/3.93/2.64 YPC. Base flow: DAL leads by a score late, keeps throwing, Williams stays near 14 carries, PHI trails without a clean rushing answer.
script.flip1: DAL scores early and leads by 14, then runs the clock. Williams' carries jump past 18 and a chunk run (PHI has allowed 16 runs of 10+ in 6 games) clears 64.5 rush and 81.5 rush+rec, while Flournoy's intermediate targets die after halftime.
script.flip2: PHI finds DAL's soft front (4.93 YPC allowed, 21 runs of 10+) and chews clock, or DAL's 28% blitz (PHI QB -0.26 EPA on 89 blitz dropbacks) turns it into a slog. DAL pass volume drops and Flournoy's over dies; Williams' under still survives because a trailing or clock-chewed DAL does not add carries.

matchup.pressure: PHI blitz rate 25%. Dak EPA 0.17 unblitzed vs 0.02 when blitzed (n=89), so he mostly sees his better split. DAL blitz rate 28%. PHI QB EPA -0.26 vs blitz vs 0.00 unblitzed (n=89). Pressure is a PHI problem. No pressure-rate-allowed or pass-rusher injury in the pack.
matchup.bleeds: DAL bleeds the middle (10.53 YPA on 38 throws) and the run (4.93 YPC, 21 runs of 10+, 22 passes of 20+ on 187 att). PHI does not bleed a side: 4.10 YPC, 16 runs of 10+ in 6 games, 19 passes of 20+ on 227 att (8.4%). Short and intermediate throws are the realistic DAL path; deep efficiency is what PHI can take away.
matchup.overlap: Best schematic overlap is PHI short/middle into DAL's middle bleed plus a 28% blitz: Goedert 5.3 aDOT and 33 rec yds/game, Lemon 4.5 aDOT and 29.7. That overlap does not clear Goedert 49.5 or Lemon 39.5, so it is a pass, not a bet. Lamb (45 targets, the primary) does not map to a PHI weak side; PHI's soundest side is right at 6.73 YPA. Flournoy's 5.6 aDOT is the DAL piece that fits the compact shell without needing a bleed.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Flournoy is the third piece of a DAL pass tree that PHI's 25% blitz will not knock off schedule, and 19 targets for 167 yards (55.7 a game, 5.6 aDOT) is priced at 34.5 against a compact defense he does not need to explode on.
edge_players.must_be_true: Week 4-6 tree holds: about 5-6 targets, Dak in the unblitzed 0.17 EPA split, game stays competitive so second-half throws do not vanish. No unlisted scratch reshuffles his routes.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip 1: DAL up big and the pass volume dies after halftime. Or the 167 yards are one spike week the aggregate hides, and PHI's 6.73-7.23 YPA shell holds him in the mid-20s.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Williams has been a 14-carry, 49.3-yard rusher plus 15.7 receiving yards, and a 4-point spread against PHI's 4.10 YPC front is not the clock-kill or the soft box that 81.5 combined yards requires.
edge_players.must_be_true: Game stays within a score, carry share stays in the low-to-mid teens, receiving stays checkdown residue (10 targets, -4 air yards over 3 games), no breakaway.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip 1: DAL leads by 14 early, Williams gets 18-plus carries and one of the 10+ runs PHI has allowed 16 times, plus a dump-off, and combined yards clear 81.5. Tagged script-dependent on that flip only.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so this is not a full step-8 price check. Available check is week 4-6 role vs the rung: Flournoy 55.7 rec yds vs 34.5 and Williams 49.3 rush + 15.7 rec = 65.0 vs 81.5 both agree. These are leans, not 70% model legs. A later sim median under ~30 for Flournoy or over ~90 for Williams would be a flag, not a silent cut; that sim is not here.

Williams rushrecyds under 81.5 at -111, not rushyds under 64.5: combined production is 65.0, so 81.5 still has room if carries tick up a few, while 64.5 rush is only 15 yards above 49.3 and dies faster on flip 1. No alt rungs in the pack. Lamb over 80 is unused; price is +nan and the gap is only 89.3 vs 80.
pre_mortem: Monday both lost because the game was the blowout, not the one-score script a +4 and 43.5 describe. DAL led by two scores at half, Flournoy's 19-target pace was cut to a handful of second-half snaps and he finished under 34.5, and Williams added a 10+ run PHI has allowed 16 times in six games plus a checkdown to clear 81.5. The Flournoy-only loss is lumpiness: no game log, so a 90-yard week inside 167 mean-reverts against a PHI pass defense with no side over 7.23 YPA. That counter is the flip and the missing split, not a stronger base case, so both stay leans and neither is strong. Barkley taking a full snap count would only rewrite PHI rush reads already passed.
slip_story: One story: competitive DAL lead, pass volume holds because PHI blitzes 25% and has not run anyone off the field, Williams does not get a clock-kill. Stack is Flournoy recyds over 34.5 with Williams rushrecyds under 81.5. They win together in the base and in flip 2's pass-volume dip only the Williams leg survives; flip 1 loses both, which is the same story failing, not two stories mixed. Do not add Pickens over 64.5 (11.7 aDOT into a defense with 19 explosives on 227 throws) or a Goedert/Lemon over (right overlap, wrong number). No TDs, one market per player, two legs.
